reviews.title: Cloudflare security-audit-skill
reviews.summary: Recommendation: ADAPT the evidence discipline, not the whole audit apparatus. The problem is familiar: an AI can produce a convincing security finding before it has established a real failure. Cloudflare separates confirmed findings, unresolved leads and rejected candidates, with different output requirements. We inspected the pinned README, findings-validator source and part of the report schema. The validator contains checks rejecting severity on unresolved findings and preventing a confirmed severity from exceeding its stated impact. That is a concrete implementation detail, not proof that the supplied evidence is true. GhostMesh already uses source review and receipts; adding another review system would duplicate machinery unless it reduces missed defects, false alarms or reviewer effort. The smallest useful comparison is to classify one existing review's findings with these rules and record what changes, without installing the skill or launching its full workflow. For an everyday user, the benefit is mostly indirect: a clearer distinction between a demonstrated problem and an alarming hypothesis. This is not a consumer security app or a substitute for expert investigation. The repository's MIT license permits reuse subject to its terms. Full use introduces a tool-using coding agent, Node.js validators and independently enforced sandbox requirements for target-controlled execution. The narrow method adaptation is small; the cost and benefit of the complete workflow remain unmeasured.
reviews.unknowns: No validator tests or audits were run by GhostMesh. We did not establish false-positive rate, missed-finding rate, reviewer-time savings, sandbox enforcement or maintenance responsiveness. Structured evidence fields cannot independently prove an exploit or make agent-written evidence trustworthy. This is not authorization to execute target code or adopt the complete harness.

ghostmeshFit.rationale: Editorial assessment: separating proved failures from unresolved leads fits existing evidence-based review. Reuse the distinction inside that process rather than add a second authority or review system.

everydayUse.rationale: Low direct usefulness for a nontechnical user. Its outputs could help someone question an overstated security claim, but operating a coding-agent audit is specialist work.

evidenceStrength.rationale: Specific verdict and severity checks are visible in source. Their runtime behavior, the quality of generated findings and actual security outcomes were not tested here.

adoptionEffort.rationale: Low only for the recommended narrow method adaptation. Full harness adoption would require separate sandbox, agent-cost and workflow evaluation; its effort is not measured.

reviews.identity: Cloudflare-maintained coding-agent audit skill for developers and security reviewers; it separates confirmed failures, unresolved leads and rejected candidates.
reviews.scope: Pinned c1c8a8c: README, findings-validator source and part of the report schema inspected. The skill, validator and audit workflow were not run.
reviews.selectionRationale: Its separation of demonstrated failures from unresolved leads speaks to GhostMesh evidence and review receipts.

reviews.title: Graphify
reviews.summary: Recommendation: EXPERIMENT, subject to separate authorization, with a small public code-only fixture. The problem is repeated rediscovery: which files call this function, and what might a change affect? Graphify documents local tree-sitter parsing, a queryable graph and distinctions between extracted and inferred relationships. For GhostMesh, that could make repository navigation cheaper, but it would remain a derived map, not the authority for ownership, permissions or completion. Its incumbent is ordinary repository search and direct source reading. A useful comparison would ask the same fixed cross-file questions using both methods, check answers against source, then repeat after a controlled source change to expose stale-graph behavior. Measure correctness, elapsed effort and refresh cost before considering integration. For an everyday user who does not work with code, direct value is limited. Document and media mapping may sound more approachable, but it changes the privacy boundary: the documentation says semantic extraction may send content to a configured model backend. The open-source repository carries Apache-2.0; the promoted hosted Cloud service is a separate offering, not evidence that the local tool delivers its advertised savings. README and security-policy review establishes the documented design, not implementation correctness. No benchmark, privacy guarantee or claimed token saving was verified.
reviews.unknowns: No parsing, graph querying, security controls or benchmarks were tested. Graph accuracy on GhostMesh repositories, refresh reliability, total maintenance effort and maintainer response quality remain unknown. The security policy acknowledges residual prompt-injection risk in semantic extraction. Do not upload private documents or enable optional network integrations on this recommendation.

ghostmeshFit.rationale: A derived cross-file map could help navigation, but it cannot replace canonical source, work ownership or live operational evidence. It must outperform existing search after including refresh effort.

everydayUse.rationale: The immediate value is for people navigating code. Broader document mapping requires technical setup and a separate decision about model-provider data exposure.

evidenceStrength.rationale: Documentation and security policy were reviewed, not the parser or query implementation. Upstream demonstrations and benchmarks are not independent GhostMesh measurements.

adoptionEffort.rationale: A bounded code-only comparison is narrower than integrating hooks, MCP or hosted services. Ongoing indexing, parser dependencies and stale-map handling still require ownership; hours and costs are unmeasured.

reviews.identity: Graphify-Labs code-mapping tool for developers and coding assistants; it documents a local graph of cross-file relationships and optional semantic mapping beyond code.
reviews.scope: Pinned 847a93f: README, security policy and license reviewed. Parser and query code were not inspected; no graph was built or measured.
reviews.selectionRationale: Repeated cross-file investigation makes a derived code map worth comparing against direct source search.

reviews.title: NVIDIA OpenShell
reviews.summary: Recommendation: WATCH before any runtime replacement. OpenShell targets a real problem: an agent that can work with files, networks and credentials needs enforceable limits, not just instructions to behave. NVIDIA documents a gateway-and-sandbox design with kernel-level controls, approved-endpoint credential handling and policy-change analysis. Those are vendor-described capabilities, not guarantees established by this review. GhostMesh already has execution and authorization boundaries. A replacement would need to preserve their useful protections while reducing operational complexity, not merely add another control plane. First compare the same allowed and denied actions, credential exposure, restart behavior and recovery requirements on paper. Any later runtime experiment would need separate authorization and isolation from working services. For an everyday user, the likely benefit is indirect, through safer agent products built on such infrastructure. It is not a one-click personal assistant. The Apache-2.0 project requires a supported operating environment plus containers or virtualization, and its README documents telemetry and opt-out controls. Adopting it would affect a consequential boundary and bring gateway, sandbox and lifecycle maintenance. Neither a well-known vendor nor a sophisticated design proves that migration would improve GhostMesh reliability.
reviews.unknowns: No enforcement implementation, sandbox escape resistance, credential isolation, policy proofs, telemetry behavior or recovery path was verified. Comparative security, total operating cost and migration effort remain unknown. This review does not establish a fix for any existing service outage or authorize infrastructure, credential or production changes.

ghostmeshFit.rationale: The documented containment problem is relevant, but replacement value depends on matching existing authority boundaries and improving lifecycle and recovery behavior.

everydayUse.rationale: Primarily infrastructure for people operating agents. Ordinary users may benefit indirectly, but installation and policy operation are not a consumer workflow.

evidenceStrength.rationale: Repository documentation, license and disclosure policy were read. Runtime containment and policy-verification claims remain untested here.

adoptionEffort.rationale: A runtime replacement affects policy, credentials, gateway operations and recovery. High is a scope judgment, not an engineering-hours estimate.

reviews.identity: NVIDIA agent runtime for teams operating autonomous agents; it documents policy-constrained file, network and credential access through gateways and sandboxes.
reviews.scope: Pinned 029fda6: README, security policy and license reviewed. Enforcement code and runtime behavior were not inspected or tested.
reviews.selectionRationale: Agent containment raises a concrete comparison with existing authority, credential and recovery boundaries.
